summary: Prewarm no-op during canary causes tenant to remain bound to legacy route after rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after a scheduled canary (weighted rollout) the tenant continued to be routed to the legacy model variant despite the canary being marked as healthy. Traffic shows pinned behavior to the older variant.

Impact:
- QuietSearch sees ~30% of their requests hitting the legacy model post-rollout which returns older tokenization (quality delta).
- Elevated per-request latency on legacy variant and slight cost increase due to fallback path triggering.
- Customer-facing: 12 users reported degraded results in a rolling window, customer flagged as urgent due to production usage.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (tenant-dedicated) in prod-us-east-1.
- Rollout used: weighted canary 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 45m window with prewarm step.
- Model variants: open-econ-3b-quant (legacy), open-econ-7b-v1 (canary).

Steps to reproduce (observed by CS and customer):
1) Start rollout with prewarm mirror to prepare GPU pool.
2) Prewarm mirror service returned 204 (no-op) for several prewarm requests due to cache warmup guard engaged.
3) Orchestrator proceeded to shift weights per schedule.
4) After canary marked healthy, ~30% tenant traffic still routed to legacy variant for ~2 hours.

Logs / telemetry attached:
- Edge routing logs show persistent route key binding to legacy variant (route_key=tenant:qs-12345) even after snapshot epoch advanced.
- Orchestrator snapshot commit entries present, but prewarm events show repeated "prewarm-noop: already-warmed" at t=03:04-03:09.
- Serving runtime metrics: hybrid-serving reported "pin-lease-renewal" success but edge cookies show older cookie path for affected connections.

Initial hypothesis:
- Prewarm no-op (guarded mirror response) left a tombstone in the prewarm metadata which prevented the edge from observing the resume handshake that clears legacy pin.
- Edge cookie scope truncation during the prewarm step caused session affinity mismatches and the tenant remained bound to old route for long-lived connections.

Requested from customer:
- Full request ids for two affected traces and a pcap of a representative stream (customer provided request-ids: rq_20260310_1142a, rq_20260310_1337b).

Notes: please avoid broad-side restarts; prefer targeted reconciliation steps described in runbook.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Triage complete. Assigned to Raj. Collected request IDs and initial logs from customer. Noted prewarm returned 204 no-op in timeline.
Raj Patel (SRE) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Creating an orchestrator snapshot pull. Suspect prewarm metadata tombstone; will query snapshot diffs and edge cookie logs.

Alex Gomez (Eng) 2026-03-11: Found a code path where prewarm-noop sets 'prewarm_tombstone=true' in in-memory metadata but commit path ignores tombstone clearing on subsequent reconcile. Preparing a small patch to clear tombstones during snapshot apply. Linking PR after validation.
QuietSearch (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed we still see 25-35% of responses from legacy model on our end between 03:00-05:00 UTC. Appreciate quick remediation.

Raj Patel (SRE) 2026-03-11: Deployed a targeted snapshot reconcile for tenant qs-12345 to edge nodes (no restart). Observed immediate reduction of legacy hits to <2% for newly established sessions. Long-lived connections still have legacy cookie scope. Will escalate cookie refresh path.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reports degraded responses have fallen to zero for new sessions. Asking Eng/SRE for permanent fix and postmortem steps.
investigation_notes:
Findings:
- Orchestrator committed the new variant snapshot at epoch 8421. Edge nodes pulled the commit, but prewarm metadata included 'tombstone' flags from the no-op prewarm responses. Snapshot apply code merged the tombstone into route metadata because tombstone clearance only happens on explicit prewarm success, not on subsequent reconciles.
- Long-lived client sessions maintained cookies with 'Path=/v1/route/legacy' which kept affinity. Edge cookie normalization code had an off-by-one that truncated cookie path when prewarm returned 204, leading to silence about commit.
- Related logs: orchestrator commit log lines 8421..8430 show tombstone merge events; edge logs show cookie-era header 'Set-Cookie: r=qs-12345; Path=/v1/route/legacy; Expires=...'.

Hypothesis validated by targeted reconcile: clearing tombstone metadata and replaying snapshot cleared routing for new sessions. Existing connections require cookie refresh—observed via metrics where persistent connections continued to route legacy for ~90-120 minutes until cookie expired or client reconnected.

Action items (short-term):
- Run tenant-scoped metadata tombstone purge on affected shard and trigger edge reconcile (done for qs-12345).
- Provide customer a proactive recommendation to rotate their client session cookies if they can perform a graceful reconnect.

Action items (long-term):
- Engineer patch: ensure snapshot apply treats prewarm-noop tombstones as idempotent and clears them on subsequent successful prewarm or explicit reconcile. PR linked.
- Fix edge cookie normalization to avoid truncation on 204 prewarm responses; add unit tests.
- Add additional telemetry: tombstone delta gauge per-tenant and a canary prewarm health metric exposed to console.
resolution:
Workaround and fix applied:
- Short-term: performed a tenant-scoped metadata tombstone purge and forced edge reconcile for qs-12345 at 2026-03-11T21:05Z. New sessions immediately routed to canary variant; legacy route hits dropped to <2% for new connections. Provided customer instructions to force reconnects for active clients.
- Medium-term: deployed orchestrator patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2147) that prevents prewarm-noop tombstones from persisting across snapshot applies and explicitly clears stale tombstones during reconcile.
- Edge cookie normalization patch scheduled in staging (PR queued).

Follow-up:
- Postmortem to be written and linked to this ticket (owner: Raj Patel).
- Add runbook step to detect prewarm-noop tombstone spikes and auto-trigger a tenant-scoped reconcile if tombstone ratio > 0.05 for more than 5 minutes.

Customer status: QuietSearch confirmed recovery for new sessions and accepted the workaround. They requested the postmortem and a timeline for the edge cookie fix; SRE/Eng will follow up with dates.
